evidence.claim: Amnesty said more than 1,500 Nigerian schoolchildren had been abducted by armed groups since Chibok and accused the authorities of failing to protect children and respond to warning alerts.
evidence.title: Eight years after Chibok, thousands of children subjected to abduction by armed groups
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said more than 1,500 Nigerian schoolchildren had been abducted by armed groups since Chibok and accused the authorities of failing to protect children and respond to warning alerts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization investigation with a specific child-protection claim and numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 domestic security environment and its inherited child-abduction crisis
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a national-level failure under Buhari's administration, though many kidnappings were carried out by non-state armed groups.
contrary_evidence: The source is advocacy-oriented and does not quantify all government rescue efforts or isolated successes.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said that between 2020 and 2022 it documented enforced disappearances, mass arrest, torture, extortion, ill-treatment, and extrajudicial executions by law enforcement officers responding to IPOB activity in the southeast and southwest.
evidence.title: Nigeria must show genuine commitment to ending enforced disappearances
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said that between 2020 and 2022 it documented enforced disappearances, mass arrest, torture, extortion, ill-treatment, and extrajudicial executions by law enforcement officers responding to IPOB activity in the southeast and southwest.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Amnesty statement tying abuses to law-enforcement responses and giving a date-bounded pattern claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These are state-agent abuses under Buhari's presidency, though the incidents may involve lower-level command chains rather than Buhari personally.
contrary_evidence: The source is a rights-advocacy statement and should be read together with more neutral reporting.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said more than 40 #EndSARS protesters were still in prison and that panels set up to investigate police impunity had failed to deliver justice to hundreds of victims of police brutality.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Two years on, more than 40 #EndSARS protesters still languishing in jail
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said more than 40 #EndSARS protesters were still in prison and that panels set up to investigate police impunity had failed to deliver justice to hundreds of victims of police brutality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-organization report with a direct detention and accountability claim.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 protest-treatment and accountability
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is about federal/state security and justice under Buhari's administration, not solely local police behavior.
contrary_evidence: The report focuses on ongoing detention and impunity and does not capture every case where protesters were released or compensated.

evidence.claim: CPJ said police arrested journalist Agba Jalingo on August 19 and moved him through multiple detention sites after a defamation and cyberattack complaint.
evidence.title: Nigerian journalist Agba Jalingo detained over defamation, cyberattack complaint
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said police arrested journalist Agba Jalingo on August 19 and moved him through multiple detention sites after a defamation and cyberattack complaint.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor with named arresting force and custody sequence, but still based on contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrest and detention are attributable to state security organs within Buhari's domestic-security system.
contrary_evidence: The CPJ report is one case and does not establish the full national media environment by itself.

evidence.claim: The NHRC said the Independent Investigative Panel awarded compensation to 100 victims of police brutality, totaling about N431.9 million, after hearing 294 cases.
evidence.title: IIP-SARS awards N431,884,094 compensation to 100 victims of police brutality
evidence.excerpt: The NHRC said the Independent Investigative Panel awarded compensation to 100 victims of police brutality, totaling about N431.9 million, after hearing 294 cases.
evidence.source_locator: search result snippet from the NHRC page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official commission announcement, though the page itself was partially blocked and the usable text comes from the indexed snippet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is remedy by a federal human-rights institution operating under Buhari's government, not evidence of Buhari's personal intervention in each case.
contrary_evidence: Compensation for some victims does not itself show that systemic police abuse ended.

evidence.claim: Buhari condemned the beheading of soldiers, called on leaders to speak with one voice against the violence, and directed security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators.
evidence.title: President Buhari Shocked, Saddened by IPOB Beheading of Soldiers
evidence.excerpt: Buhari condemned the beheading of soldiers, called on leaders to speak with one voice against the violence, and directed security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential statement directly addressing a domestic violent incident and the state response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari's public stance and security direction.
contrary_evidence: The statement condemns violence but does not itself demonstrate effective prevention or accountability.

evidence.claim: HRW said 2022 insecurity included the killing of 40 worshippers in Owo, the Kuje prison attack, and the Abuja-Kaduna train attack, and that Nigerian authorities responding to the threats were also implicated in abuses.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: HRW said 2022 insecurity included the killing of 40 worshippers in Owo, the Kuje prison attack, and the Abuja-Kaduna train attack, and that Nigerian authorities responding to the threats were also implicated in abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent annual rights report with direct summaries of the year's major incidents and state-response concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These are security outcomes under Buhari's government; the attacks were perpetrated by non-state actors, while the abuses implicated state responders.
contrary_evidence: HRW is a rights monitor and emphasizes abuse and impunity, so it should be read alongside more neutral incident reporting.

evidence.claim: In September, Nigeria signed a handover protocol with the UN agreeing that children taken into military custody on suspicion of Boko Haram involvement should be transferred within seven days to civilian authorities for reintegration.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Nigeria
evidence.excerpt: In September, Nigeria signed a handover protocol with the UN agreeing that children taken into military custody on suspicion of Boko Haram involvement should be transferred within seven days to civilian authorities for reintegration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent annual rights report summarizing a concrete child-protection and custody reform step.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 institutional reform and child protection
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a federal reform step under Buhari's government, though not necessarily a presidentially managed operational action.
contrary_evidence: The protocol is a reform measure, not proof that detention or recruitment abuses had already ended.
